lesenParts.textTitle: Rising Star: An Interview with Leo Vance
lesenParts.text:
At just sixteen, Leo Vance has already made a name for himself in the world of competitive swimming. We caught up with him at his local training centre in Manchester. 'I started swimming when I was five,' Leo explains, drying off after a two-hour morning session. 'My parents took me to the pool every weekend, but I didn't really take it seriously until I joined a club at ten.'

Leo’s routine is demanding. He wakes up at 4:30 a.m. to be in the water by 5:15 a.m. 'It’s tough, especially in winter when it's dark and cold outside,' he admits. 'But when you’re in the pool, you forget the time. You just focus on your strokes.' Despite the hard work, Leo insists he has a normal social life. 'People think athletes don't have time for friends, but I make sure I see my mates on Friday nights. It’s important to switch off.'

His biggest challenge so far was the National Youth Championships last year. 'I was so nervous before the final race,' he recalls. 'I almost pulled out, but my coach reminded me why I started. I ended up winning silver.' That medal changed his perspective. 'It wasn't just about the prize; it was about proving to myself that I could handle the pressure.'

Looking ahead, Leo has his sights set on the international stage. 'The dream is the Olympics, obviously. But for now, I’m focused on improving my technique. My coach says I’m strong, but my turns need work.' When asked if he has any advice for other young athletes, he is humble. 'Don't let the sport define who you are. Enjoy it, work hard, but remember to have fun. If you stop enjoying it, you’ll never reach your potential.'

lesenParts.textTitle: A Weekend at the Local Food Market
lesenParts.text: Last Saturday, I decided to visit the new food market in the town square. I had heard many people talking about the fresh produce and the friendly atmosphere. (1) __________ I arrived just as the stalls were opening, so it was still quite quiet. The smell of freshly baked bread and roasted coffee beans was everywhere. I walked slowly past the different stalls, looking at the colourful vegetables and local cheeses. (2) __________ I eventually stopped at a small stall that sold homemade honey. The owner was very kind and let me taste three different types before I made my choice. After buying a jar of honey, I felt hungry and looked for something to eat. (3) __________ It was filled with fresh herbs and local vegetables. It was probably the best lunch I have had in a long time. While I was eating, a local band started playing some relaxing music near the fountain. (4) __________ Many families were sitting on the grass, enjoying the sunshine and the music. It was a perfect way to spend a Saturday morning. I will definitely return next weekend to try some of the other delicious treats. (5) __________ It is a great addition to our town and I hope it stays for a long time.

lesenParts.text: Every year, thousands of music fans travel to the countryside for the Sunny Beats Festival. It is one of the most popular events in the region, and tickets often sell out months in advance. The festival (1) ______ place over three days in July, offering a wide variety of musical styles ranging from rock to electronic dance music. Many people choose to camp on-site, which allows them to fully (2) ______ the atmosphere of the event. There are several stages, so festival-goers can easily move between them to see their favourite bands. Food stalls are available everywhere, serving delicious snacks from all over the world. If you are (3) ______ of going this year, make sure to book your accommodation early as nearby hotels fill up very quickly. Organisers have also (4) ______ a new shuttle bus service to help people get to the site more easily. It is a fantastic way to (5) ______ new music and meet people who share your interests. Don't forget to bring comfortable shoes, as you will (6) ______ a lot of time walking between the different stages!

lesenParts.textTitle: A Family Trip to the Mountains
lesenParts.text: Last summer, my family and I decided to spend a week in the mountains. We had never been there before, so we were all very excited. We packed our bags and left early on Saturday morning. The drive was long, but the scenery was beautiful. When we arrived, we checked into a small wooden cabin. It was perfect (1) _____ us. The next day, we went hiking. My father wanted to climb the highest peak, but my mother preferred to stay near the lake. In the end, we made (2) _____ compromise and chose a path that went through the forest. It was quite challenging (3) _____ times, but we enjoyed every moment. During the trip, we saw many interesting animals, including a deer. We also took lots of photos (4) _____ show our friends back home. On our last night, we sat outside and looked at the stars. It was (5) _____ most peaceful experience I have ever had. We all agreed (6) _____ we would definitely like to return next year.

questions.question: Gap 1
questions.explanation: The preposition 'for' is required after the adjective 'perfect' to indicate who the cabin was suitable for.

questions.question: Gap 2
questions.explanation: The phrase 'make a compromise' is the correct collocation.

questions.question: Gap 5
questions.explanation: The superlative adjective 'most peaceful' requires the definite article 'the'.

questions.question: Gap 6
questions.explanation: The phrase 'next year' refers to the following year.

questions.question: Gap 4
questions.explanation: The phrase 'lots of' is used to indicate a large quantity.

questions.question: Gap 3
questions.explanation: The expression 'at times' means occasionally.

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 4.
horenParts.transcript: Interviewer: Today we are talking to Sarah Jenkins, who recently opened her own restaurant at just twenty-two. Sarah, was it always your dream to be a chef? Sarah: Actually, no. I wanted to be a musician, but I loved cooking for friends. Then, I took a summer job in a kitchen and realised I preferred the heat of the stove to the stage! Interviewer: Was it difficult to start your own business so young? Sarah: The hardest part wasn't the cooking, but the paperwork. I spent weeks talking to banks and finding the right location. I almost gave up once, but my mentor encouraged me to keep going. Interviewer: What is the most popular dish on your menu? Sarah: Definitely the spicy vegetable stew. I thought people would find it too hot, but they love it. I use a secret spice mix from my grandmother. Interviewer: What do you do when you are not working? Sarah: I try to get away from food entirely! I go hiking or read books. If I stay in the kitchen too long, I lose my creativity. Interviewer: What advice would you give to other young people? Sarah: Don't be afraid to make mistakes. Every burnt meal is a lesson.
